prompt_en: A cinematic documentary photograph of a woman wearing wearable robotic equipment, caught in field work with robotic equipment on the service deck of a wind-battered rooftop greenhouse. Use the supplied reference for her visible facial appearance and dark bob haircut. Her face keeps the reference's soft oval shape, dark eyes and fine wispy fringe; wind lifts a few short strands across one cheek. Her quiet concentration and relaxed mouth give the working portrait a subtle personal warmth. A heavy relay-cabinet door has been bent by the storm. Its lower edge has just settled onto a low maintenance trestle while she holds its outer handle steady, keeping a wind-blown door from swinging back across her work. The open cabinet and its displaced hinge bracket remain immediately behind the door; one loose fastener and a short wrench rest on the trestle beside the lower corner. She is checking the upper hinge alignment, with her left fingertips placed on the cabinet-side hinge bracket. Her right hand encloses the door handle, her right elbow bent naturally. An articulated utility exoskeleton follows the outside of that right arm, with a padded upper-arm cuff, an elbow pivot, a forearm cuff and a shoulder support attached to a fitted torso harness. The right-arm assembly and her human wrist remain visually distinct. Her boots are planted apart on the wet nonslip deck, and the trestle carries the door's lower edge. She wears a weathered ochre work coverall, its functional waist and rolled cuffs following her movement. Broken cloud gives soft directional daylight, a warmer sunbreak briefly touching her cheek and the pale aluminum links. Wet greenhouse glass and rows of bowed green plants give the gust a visible consequence in the background. A close full-length vertical photograph from her front-right, with enough depth of field to keep her face, the complete arm support, the handle and both door hinges readable together. Real skin and work-worn mechanical surfaces, restrained color, a particular task caught in progress.

An open shoulder harness presents its exposed root at the front outer edge of her left shoulder. A rigid exposed bracket runs continuously from that harness root to a clearly bounded upper-arm cuff, with both fixed joints facing the camera. An external elbow hinge visibly links that upper-arm cuff to a forearm cuff along the same outer side. Her bare human wrist continues beyond the forearm cuff into her left hand, visibly distinct from the end of the frame. Her left elbow is mildly bent and held clear of her ribs; air gaps separate the frame from the torso, and the whole external route faces the camera. The left palm lies across the broad lever handle; the palm edge touching its top surface, thumb beside the handle and handle entering the clamp are visible together. Her other hand hangs freely on image-left. The camera sees her from slightly in front of her left side, framed from head to mid-thigh with space around the entire shoulder-to-handle route. Broad window light models her face and gives each mechanical connection an edged highlight against a subdued workshop background. The face, linked arm support and hand contact carry the photograph together, with natural skin texture and restrained metallic reflections.
